detail.abstract: This thesis presents three essays on the Öeld of personal bankruptcy. The research carried out is mostly, but not fully, theoretical in nature. The Örst chapter develops a model of general equilibrium with default and asks, among other things, how the level of default penalties can a§ect the welfare of di§erent agents in an economy, when do agents face binding borrowing limits, and why some agents are denied credit upon application. In answer to these questions, it shows that there exists an intermediate range of Pareto optimal punishment levels where changes in the punishment level beneÖt one type of agent but harm another; outside this range, punishment levels can be changed to beneÖt all agents. It also proves that the existence of default is a su¢ cient condition for the emergence of borrowing limits which are binding; asymmetric information is not necessary for this to occur. Finally, is shows that some agents can be denied credit if default penalties are too low or too high. In these instances, it shows that even though these agents would like to borrow at the market interest rates, they are unable to do so. The chapter then also asks whether a competitive market will select the socially optimal punishment level, and shows that this is not, in general, the case - welfare can be improved if default penalties are set by a social planner. Finally, a numerical experiment is performed to evaluate the welfare e§ects of a change in the law which allows only low-income households to Öle for default on their debts. The result shows the welfare e§ects of this will depend on the degree of agent heterogeneity; if the gap between rich agents and poor agents is not large, then this policy beneÖts all agents. If however the gap between the rich and the poor is substantially large, then this policy will beneÖt those who save and rich agents who borrow, while harming poor agents who borrow. This illustrates the importance of agent heterogeneity when evaluating di§erent policies in bankruptcy legislation under a general equilibrium setting. Following this, we argue that the welfare evaluations from various studies of bankruptcy may be biased upwards if they do not allow for enough heterogeneity among agents. The second chapter extends this model to a world consisting of many open economies from between which funds can be transferred without cost, and examines how default penalties are set endogenously by the governments of each region. It then explores the implications of such endogenous punishment formation. From a normative perspective, it asks whether the resulting non-cooperative Nash equilibrium is welfare-maximising. We Önd that this is not in general the case, and that welfare can increase if governments set their punishment levels cooperatively. From a positive point of view, it compares the e§ect of an exogenous shock in income distributions to the equilibrium allocations in the case of Öxed punishment levels and in the case of variable punishment levels (i.e. the case when governments are able to react to a change in the economic environment by altering bankruptcy legislation). The analysis shows that allowing for endogenous punishment levels can reverse the results of such exogenous shocks. For example, one of the puzzles in the literature is that default rates have been increasing, despite rising incomes. We show that, keeping punishments Öxed, higher incomes result in more borrowing but less default. However, when we allow punishments to vary endogenously, these fall in response to higher incomes and the result is more borrowing and more default. Finally, the third chapter develops the model to include bankruptcy exemptions which resemble legislation in the US and examines how these should be set optimally in a partial equilibrium environment. It then studies how optimal exemption levels depend on various economic variables. It derives a simple rule in a completely general environment which states that any exogenous shock which increases the level of borrowing implies a higher optimal exemption level. For example, all else equal, higher (future) incomes imply higher levels of borrowing. Therefore, economies with higher incomes should have higher exemption levels. It then tests this empirically using data from the US, where exemption levels vary between states. The main innovation from the empirical part with respect to similar studies is that the analysis controls for neighbourhood e§ects in the sense that states may take into account the exemption levels in neighbouring states when setting their own exemption level.

detail.abstract: Randomized controlled trials in economics rarely report participant flow diagrams, and when they do the reasons for losses to follow-up are not given. We argue that transparent attrition reporting provides important public goods by unlocking underpowered, high-stakes policy endpoints-such as maternal and child mortality, school dropouts, job loss, eviction or incarceration. We demonstrate how such outcomes, unobservable in individual studies, can be detected in meta-analysis. Unlike many other reported outcomes, these measurements suffer from negligible recall, reporting or publication biases. Transparent participant flow reporting avoids the great opportunity costs of lost attrition data for evidence-based policy, at minimal administrative cost.

detail.abstract: Legal theories examine validity, interpretation, proof, and institutional authority, yet legal reasoning can compress human circumstances into an isolated fact and treat the resulting decision as the end of inquiry. Developed from the Theory of Human Centrality (TCH), the Amphianthropic Theory of Law (ATL) proposes a six-stage architecture: Human Formation, Human Antecedence, Fact, Value, Norm/Decision, and Human Consequence. The latter may shape future human conditions, creating a recursive legal process. ATL preserves normative autonomy and makes external expertise conditional on relevance, reliability, materiality, necessity, and proportionality. This foundational manuscript compares major jurisprudential alternatives, examines judicial and legislative materials from eight countries, articulates five contestable hypotheses, and illustrates applications across ten legal fields. It further proposes three legally bounded analytical mechanisms: an audit of epistemic limits, a counterfactual test for materially omitted human dimensions, and a review of consequences where institutional competence permits continuing action. These mechanisms are situated against existing scholarship in legal epistemology, causal inference, and structural remedies rather than presented as discoveries without predecessors. Head-to-head conceptual comparisons identify possible incremental contributions, cases of doctrinal redundancy, negative controls, and conditions for empirical refutation. The manuscript does not report controlled experiments or claim demonstrated superiority over competing theories. Its contribution is a comparative research programme for evaluating whether a structured before-and-after analysis improves legally relevant understanding without sacrificing rights, institutional limits, or proportionality.

detail.abstract: Public libraries have increasingly shifted their collections toward digital formats, raising important questions about how e-book lending affects commercial book markets and the broader publishing ecosystem. This study examines the relationship between public library e-lending and retail book sales using three complementary empirical approaches. First, a state-level analysis covering 2013-2023 evaluates whether increases in the digital share of public library collections are associated with changes in print book sales. Second, a title-level analysis combines lending data from the Seattle Public Library with local retail sales data to estimate substitution between library borrowing and consumer purchases. Third, a bestseller model links library availability, national sales data, and Google Trends measures of consumer demand to assess the relationship between e-lending and e-book sales for nationally prominent titles. Across these distinct empirical frameworks, the results consistently indicate that greater library e-book availability is associated with statistically significant reductions in retail book sales, suggesting that e-lending functions, at least in part, as a substitute for commercial purchases rather than solely as a mechanism for discovery. The estimated effects are generally strongest for titles earlier in their commercial lifecycle and in categories where consumers are most likely to substitute between borrowing and purchasing. The study also evaluates the broader economic implications of these findings through input-output modeling, demonstrating that reductions in trade book sales may extend beyond authors and publishers to affect employment, labor income, output, and tax revenues. Taken together, the results provide new empirical evidence on the interaction between public library e-lending and commercial book markets and offer an economic framework for evaluating digital licensing policies and proposed legislative interventions.

detail.abstract: This paper studies rational bubbles in an uncertain trading network and compares price-taking and strategic intermediaries. A network bubble requires at least three states and five agents, and the lower-bound argument extends to higher-order bubbles. Whether these bounds are attainable depends on traders' behavior. Under price taking, five agents require a fourth state and a knife-edge restriction on the prior because competitive prices reveal information needed for subsequent resale. Under strategic bilateral trading, by contrast, three states and five agents suffice, attaining the lower bounds. Furthermore, even when prices and actions are publicly observable, the bubble can be sustained for every full-support prior because sellers can pool offers across states to preserve resale opportunities. The examples also suggest that strategic behavior may redistribute surplus relative to price taking. Thus, traders' strategic behavior can reshape the informational requirements for a rational bubble and, in turn, the distribution of trading surplus.

detail.abstract: ​We introduce Purpose-Governed Recursive Invariant Discovery, a comprehensive six-layer operational architecture designed for ontological grounding, recursive refinement, fixed-point analysis, and machine-verifiable scientific inquiry. Built upon a WAD-18 exact integer arithmetic substrate that eliminates floating-point ambiguity, the framework establishes a rigorous epistemic state machine, machine-executable decision contracts, and a recursive engine capable of systematically decomposing complex systems, isolating invariant properties, and recomposing verified models without silent failures or ungrounded assumptions. Operating under a strict governing mandate where every material claim must terminate in a proof obligation, evidence record, or explicit unresolved state, the architecture provides a robust blueprint for prospective, falsifiable scientific research, demonstrated through structured test cases including collective quantum states and room-temperature superconductivity, ensuring that all derived insights remain strictly traceable, reproducible, and bound by empirical evidence.

detail.abstract: A mineral can be essential to a growing industrial use and still leave almost no measurable trace in the listed companies associated with it. This paper sets out the Stockatomics Constraint Transmission Framework, a mineral-first specification for connecting downstream demand to the difficulty of expanding or replacing supply, to concentration at a stated production stage, and to the production exposure of listed issuers. The mineral is the stable unit. Sectors and products explain demand. Companies enter only through a compatible measure of current output. The specification separates four objects that thematic research usually collapses: structural supply responsiveness, a scenario-dependent demand outlook, concentration, and company participation in supply. Supply responsiveness is summarised by the Supply Elasticity Score (SES), an equal-weighted composite of lead time, capital intensity, processing bottlenecks, substitution difficulty and recycling difficulty. Despite the name, SES is not an econometric elasticity. Demand Momentum (DM) is a growth rate under stated sector shares. The Demand Pressure Score (DPS) is the normalised demand term used inside company scores. Mineral Exposure (MES), Supply Leverage (SLS) and the Critical Mineral Catalyst Score (CMCS) aggregate production shares against those mineral conditions. The aggregation identities are stated in full. Component rubrics and the fixed bounds that map raw sums onto 0-100 remain versioned implementation parameters. A constructed numerical case shows why two minerals with the same SES can imply different adjustment paths, and why a demand revision moves the indicators of a verified producer without creating production exposure for a developer or a cost exposure for a buyer. The paper specifies data requirements, known weaknesses in the current database, and a programme of validity, sensitivity and outcome tests. It does not estimate a production network, does not establish that demand exceeds supply, and does not claim that the scores predict equity returns.

detail.abstract: The emergence of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) marks a significant geopolitical rupture in West Africa, with military regimes in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger systematically expelling Western influence. While the military and economic aspects of this realignment have been thoroughly dissected in contemporary study, the language mechanics of the juntas' statecraft remain critically underexamined. This study fills this gap by examining how anti-imperial discourse serves not only as populist grievance, but as a purposeful architectural tool of sovereign statecraft. Employing Norman Fairclough's Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), this study uses a selected eight-text corpus of primary institutional treaties and top-level diplomatic speeches from the leadership of the Sahel. The empirical findings show how the AES weaponizes discursive methods and cross-border digital information warfare to create domestic legitimacy and destroy the current regional order. Their key tactics include the semantic inversion of branding Paris as the "French junta" to strip the former colonial power of its democratic authority, and the mobilization of Sankarist intertextuality to frame unconstitutional seizures of power as authentic generational liberation. Furthermore, the analysis shows how this anti-imperial stance is legally enshrined in the Confederation Treaty to delegitimize the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and its procedural rules. This research ultimately indicates that the AES's "rhetoric of rupture" functions as a carefully calculated tool for the survival of authoritarian regimes. While this discourse successfully deconstructs the neocolonial architecture of Françafrique, it also performs an ideological shielding function that masks the rise of new, highly transactionalized militarized dependencies with actors such as Russia and Turkey, while systematically criminalizing domestic democratic opposition as foreign-sponsored treason.

detail.abstract: Both pure altruism and the warm-glow motive for charitable giving possess significant theoretical limitations. Given that donations typically support vulnerable populations, this study explores how the remorse of conscience and guilt serve as primary motives, utilizing a model of conscience where individuals cooperate to achieve the "benefit of a group as a whole" (BGW). Within this framework, collective benefits allow individuals to naturally cooperate without triggering the prisoner's dilemma. Furthermore, because institutional imperfections cause individuals to unintentionally or passively behave opportunistically, they donate to offset these behaviors, driven by remorse and guiltparticularly under high levels of conscience. Finally, by incorporating the framework of sustainable heterogeneity (SH), this study demonstrates that substantial financial contributions by a small number of wealthy households are neither incomprehensible nor anomalous, but rather represent highly rational behavior.

detail.abstract: Gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) is the most commonly accessed form of medical gender-affirmation, yet little is known about its labor market consequences. Leveraging linked administrative data for more than 12,000 transgender Australians who initiated testosterone-based or estrogen-based GAHT between 2015 and 2025, we provide the first causal evidence on these effects. Using a stacked event study design that compares earlier to later initiators of the same age and sex assigned at birth over a ten-year window, we find that estrogen-based GAHT leads to a widening and persistent earnings penalty, averaging 18% over the first five years of treatment. This earnings penalty is accompanied by a 6.7 percentage point drop in employment that explains approximately three-quarters of the reduced earnings. In contrast, testosterone-based GAHT leads to a temporary earnings penalty that peaks at 12% in the third year, after which earnings return to pre-treatment trends despite a gradual decline in employment that reaches 5.0 percentage points by the fifth year. The results are robust to comparing individuals who initiate GAHT just seven to nine months apart, a gap which plausibly reflects differences in appointment availability. Mechanism analyses point to three potential channels: job search induced by employer discrimination, newly recognized health conditions, and household disruptions. Estimates for all three channels are larger in magnitude among transfeminine people, which, together with increased working hours among employed transmasculine people, may explain the diverging earnings trajectories.

detail.abstract: Did India convert the U.S.–China tariff shock into lasting export gains? This paper examines 95,868 U.S. HTS8 product-year observations for 2015–2023, combining import values with Section 301 treatment histories and India’s 2015–2017 revealed comparative advantage. It separates initial adjustment in 2018–2019, the pandemic-transition period in 2020–2021, and strict persistence in 2022– 2023. Observed-pair cohort-time comparisons do not establish a broad positive Indian gain relative to never-threatened products, either initially or in the strict period. Continuous tariff-intensity regressions show a positive Indian association under HS2-by-year controls, but the strict-period coefficient falls from 0.204 to 0.044 log points per ten tariff percentage points under HS4-by-year controls and becomes imprecise. China’s negative exposure relationship remains robust across this fixed-effect hierarchy. The preferred capability interaction is positive but uncertain, and neither it nor its changefrom the initial period establishes capability-led persistence. Pooled estimates are consistent with stronger relative growth among other non-China suppliers, although this attenuates under within-sector overlap restrictions. Sparse, concentrated controls and nonrandom tariff targeting limit causal interpretation. The findings show a robust negative relationship between tariff exposure and U.S. imports from China, alongside suggestive, specification-sensitive Indian gains. Persistence is evaluated under continuing tariffs; the results do not establish competitiveness after tariff removal or physical production relocation.

detail.abstract: Two people can know everything relevant, hold fixed preferences, lose nothing by asking, and still be right to answer "not yet". In a complete-information game, two parties can ratify a relationship on fixed terms, keep building, or leave. Building changes the state, and so the value of ratifying, but only if both take part. Within the relationship, equilibrium payoffs are unique. Building before ratifying can be strictly optimal. The obstacle lies between the parties: what would make ratification worthwhile has yet to be built, and neither can build it alone. When only one is ready, the reluctant one is indispensable but not sovereign: if its preferred path is financed from some such state, it characterizes all productive entry there. Patience cuts both ways. A better starting state can rule out entry; when refusal risks the relationship, making it safer can eliminate entry, then restore it.

detail.abstract:
Advanced Intelligence depends on two inputs whose contributions are recognised in many contexts but are not consistently connected to the AI services they enable. Collective knowledge is supported by public research, education, scientific infrastructure and intellectual property, yet a common framework for describing the collective knowledge foundation of a particular service remains insufficiently developed. Electricity is metered, certified and reported for facilities and organisations, yet it is not consistently disclosed at the level of a defined AI service. This paper describes the resulting challenge as an accounting gap in the Advanced Intelligence economy.

Building on the WAIA White Paper, this paper develops two instruments. Human Knowledge Capital is an analytical category for collective knowledge contributions, refined through a four-layer taxonomy and the concepts of Unattributed Capital and Knowledge Rent. The Watt Standard is a proposed service-level reporting framework that brings together physical electricity consumption, energy-procurement claims and per-service electricity intensity for a defined AI service. The extent to which existing instruments provide these elements in one integrated service-level disclosure remains to be established through systematic comparison with relevant literature, technical standards and reporting practices. The proposed framework's added value must be tested through that comparison and a pilot study.

The paper contributes a reporting template—the Watt Record—a staged implementation pathway and a set of testable research questions. It does not claim that collective knowledge has a single measurable price, that energy use measures the value of knowledge, or that recognising a contribution automatically justifies collecting revenue.

detail.abstract: Academic research has shown throughout the years the ability of technical indicators to convey predictive value, informational content, and practical use. The popularity of such studies goes in and out over the years and today is being recognized widely by behavioral economists. Automated technical analysis is said to detect geometric and nonlinear shapes in prices which ordinary time series methods would be unable to detect. Previous papers use smoothing estimators to detect such patterns. Our paper uses local polynomial regressions, digital image processing, and state of the art machine learning tools to detect the patterns. Our results show that they are nonrandom, convey informational value, and have some predictive ability. We validate our results with prior works using stocks from the Dow Jones Industrial Average for a sample period from 1925-2019 using daily price observations.

detail.abstract: We explore the role of migration-related fear infear in predicting exchange rate volatility for Germany, France, and the United Kingdom within the generalized autoregressive conditional heteroscedastic (GARCH) mixed-data sampling (MIDAS) framework, using the United States dollar (USD) as the reference currency. While we adopt the quarterly Migration Fear Index and daily exchange rate of Euro (for France and Germany) and GBP (for the UK) to USD for the nexus between migration anxiety and exchange rate volatility, we equally augment our model with Migration Policy Uncertainty (MPU) to examine the joint predictability of the two migration fears proxies on exchange rate volatility. We conduct an empirical analysis covering the full sample period, which is further partitioned into pre-and post-GFC periods, to assess whether the nexus is sensitive to crisis. We find evidence that migration fears predict exchange rate volatility, albeit with differing outcomes. In particular, heightened migration concerns are associated with increased volatility in Euro area currencies, while the British pound exhibits a distinct response pattern. Additionally, migration fears can heighten volatility persistence, with implications for foreign exchange management, particularly for the countries in question.

detail.abstract: Referral programs are commonly treated as customer-acquisition tools. We show that, in lending markets, they can also embed loans in social relationships that support repayment after origination. Using data from a large digital lender in India, we find that referred applicants are more likely to receive credit and, conditional on approval, less likely to default. Comparing the same borrower across lenders in credit-bureau data, we find no relative approval advantage at the referring lender, but a 3.8-percentage-point reduction in default. Call-detail records show that referrer-borrower communication rises around repayment dates. Together, these findings suggest that referrals activate relationship-specific disciplining that improves repayment. We develop a model of referral contracts in which the lender screens for referrers with greater disciplining capacity and incentivizes them to exert effort. Consistent with data, the optimal contract uses default-contingent reductions in future credit access to screen and motivate referrers, with compensation paid upfront. The model yields sufficient statistics for program scale and the mix of referral incentives.

detail.abstract: Structural causal interpretation requires an information set rich enough to preserve the causal relations of the data-generating process. We examine whether statistical adequacy can assess this requirement. We distinguish closedness, whereby observed variables admit a finite-order VAR representation, from completeness, whereby an estimated structural model retains a valid causal interpretation. Using graphical representations of structural VAR systems, we characterize the causal configurations involving observed and omitted variables compatible with each property. We establish that closedness is necessary but insufficient for completeness: statistical inadequacy can rule out completeness, but statistical adequacy cannot establish it. We show that closedness violations can be empirically elusive when omitted-variable dynamic effects decay rapidly across lags. Monte Carlo simulations and a US macroeconomic application demonstrate that non-closed systems can appear well represented by low-order VARs. Finally, causal interpretation of a specific relation can be preserved under substantially weaker causal requirements.

detail.abstract: This paper compares the accuracy and computational cost of local solution methods for dynamic stochastic general equilibrium models. We study Taylor projection, dynamic perturbation, and perturbation continuation in models of stochastic growth, labor search, monetary policy, multi-country real business cycles, and asset pricing. We examine first-and second-order approximations and show that analytical integration can be used to evaluate expectations, reducing computational costs. Across all models, the local solution methods are more accurate than perturbation solutions of the same order, and second-order local methods improve on first-order local methods. Second-order dynamic perturbation is the most accurate method in this comparison, while second-order perturbation continuation delivers the most favorable trade-off between accuracy and computational cost.

detail.abstract: How does the cross-sectional filter of a trend-following portfolio determine its Sharpe ratio and its convexity, and can a filter raise the first without giving up the second? In a Gaussian benchmark, the return of any filter is a weighted sum of independent single-market trend followers, weighted by the eigenvalues of the filter times the correlation matrix. For the classic equal-risk portfolio, convexity breadth never exceeds Sharpe breadth: 73 futures markets offer about fifteen independent Sharpe bets but only four convexity bets, and skewness stops falling at about 16 markets. Targeting the volatility of current positions removes most of the remaining convexity. The Sharpe-optimal filter weights directions by trend premium and earns lead-lag premia. Estimated by a risk-premium PCA, it raises the walk-forward Sharpe ratio from 0.60 to 1.33 with no detectable loss of convexity; net of costs, it nearly matches a volatility-targeted reference system but keeps the skewness that the target removes.

detail.abstract: Objective: this research study investigates how indirect taxes have influenced the economic progress of Mauritania from 1980 to 2022. The data is gathered from the National Demographic and Economic Census Agency of Mauritania and the World Bank portal. Results: The findings demonstrate a lasting association between taxes, trade and GDP expansion. Indirect taxes have played a role in shaping the scenario by financing government expenses on infrastructure and public amenities thereby enhancing actual production and per capita economic advancement. detail.abstract: The development of digital commerce has made halal products more accessible to consumers, while also creating information asymmetries between sellers and buyers. Transparency accompanied by verification mechanisms and seller accountability may help consumers make more informed decisions. This article proposes a conceptual framework linking information asymmetry, transparency, accountability, trust, and purchase decisions. The framework still requires empirical testing and should take into account product characteristics, digital literacy, and the effectiveness of oversight.

detail.abstract: Technical analysis and machine learning offer complementary approaches to the classification of financial market behavior. Traditional technical analysis relies on the identification of recurring price patterns, while machine learning provides methods for transforming observed market information into representations that can be evaluated systematically. This paper reviews the application of support vector machines (SVMs) to financial classification, connecting prior research on stock-market forecasting and technical-pattern recognition with a proposed image-based, two-class classification framework. The discussion considers the role of SVM decision boundaries, kernel functions, and probabilistic calibration, including Platt scaling, in distinguishing between alternative market outcomes. It also considers the use of numerical price-pattern detection and chart-image representations as alternative approaches to encoding market information. The proposed framework treats visual price patterns as structured inputs whose pixel values or derived features may be used to train a binary classifier. An illustrative two-class example and Mathematica-based computational materials provide a foundation for describing the methodology. The framework is intended to support reproducible investigation of whether image-derived representations contain useful classification information beyond conventional technical indicators. Its predictive effectiveness, generalizability, and practical investment value require empirical testing using chronological out-of-sample evaluation, appropriate benchmarks, and controls for look-ahead bias and transaction costs.

detail.abstract: The United States has designated the Tren de Aragua a Foreign Terrorist Organization, expanded federal task forces against it, and charged several hundred people linked to the group. Federal officials nevertheless acknowledge that arrests represent only a small fraction of the group's presence, and no official count of its members exists. This paper argues that the central gap is not legal authority or enforcement capacity but human intelligence. The people who know most about the Tren de Aragua in American cities are its victims and the Venezuelan and Latin American communities in which it operates: migrants who pay extortion, women exploited in sex trafficking, tenants of buildings the group controls, and former members who want out. These are also the people least likely to speak to authorities, because they fear retaliation, distrust police from experience in their home countries, and fear immigration consequences. Those who do decide to report often cannot get through to an agency able to act on what they know. Drawing on the author's experience as a former organized crime prosecutor on the Colombia-Venezuela border, the paper proposes a victim-centered human intelligence framework built on five source categories, including justice and security professionals, both in partner countries and in exile, who fought these groups, the existing legal tools that protect cooperating victims and witnesses, and a cycle that links preventive and reactive action. It extends the framework to offenders who imitate the group's methods without belonging to it, warns against labeling migrants as gang members on weak indicators, and outlines cooperation with partner countries in Latin America. Building on criminological and criminalistic doctrine and on the lessons of the terrorist designation, it sets out the safeguards that allow human-source information to withstand judicial challenge and warns that extortion victims may now fear the material support bar. It then sets out the return for federal agencies: fewer victims through earlier intervention, lower cost per case through precision and unpaid victim cooperation, a digital verification layer that filters false information, and enforcement focused on identified criminals rather than on migrant communities as a whole. The paper closes with safeguards and recommendations for federal, state, and local agencies. Declaration of Generative AI Use. This paper is based on the author's own research, prosecutorial experience, and prior publications. detail.abstract: This paper compares allocations under monopoly and perfect competition in markets with adverse selection, such as insurance markets. We show that market power reduces coverage for individuals with low enough willingness to pay for insurance while increasing it for those with high enough willingness to pay. Under weak conditions, a monopolist always excludes a positive share of customers, whereas competitive firms provide coverage bounded away from zero to all customers. By contrast, to avoid cream skimming, competitive firms offer less coverage to high-willingness-to-pay consumers than a monopolist. Using simulations based on an empirical model of preferences and costs, we find that both effects are quantitatively significant. We also establish regularity properties that facilitate the analysis of competitive equilibrium with multidimensional types.

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) make codified knowledge abundant, which makes attention the scarce resource in professional work. We argue that ambiguity absorption is the mechanism through which LLMs allocate attention. A model settles the ambiguity of a request toward the modal reading in its training data and transmits the result without marking that a choice was made, so that neither the model nor its user attends to the alternatives. Building on March and Simon's (1958) uncertainty absorption and the attention-based view of the firm (Ocasio, 1997), we show that absorption economizes attention when the modal reading is right and misallocates it when it is not. Professional advantage in human-AI teams lies in recovering attention to material ambiguity. It takes four forms. Direction focuses attention on the purpose of the work. Vigilance notices when the standard reading may not fit the case. Disambiguation situates attention in the particulars of the case. Orchestration distributes attention across people, agents, and time. We derive implications for designing agentic systems and for sustaining professional expertise.

detail.abstract: Public goods experiments give subjects a fixed endowment and observe how much of it is contributed. Outside the laboratory, income must be earned before it is spent, and a household that cannot individually increment a public good has little reason to earn the income it would have devoted to that good. Free riding thus occurs in two markets: the output market, where contributions are withheld, and the input market, where the income that would have financed them is never generated. This paper shows that the input-market margin is invisible in earnedendowment as well as fixed-endowment designs, because linear payoffs make the decision to earn independent of the public good. A laboratory model with diminishing marginal value of private consumption restores the link. It predicts that a binding majority vote raises work effort for every subject, that the increase depends on whether the vote precedes or follows the work, and that voters choose more of the public good when the tax is paid from earned rather than fixed income. A six-treatment design is proposed to test these predictions. With equal tax shares, majority rule attains the efficient quantity when valuations are symmetrically distributed but underprovides when they are right-skewed.

detail.abstract: This essay examines sexual activity as a complex legal fact with consequences for the rights, duties, and legal positions of those involved. It considers a proposed descriptive distinction between the "first participant" and the "secondary participant"; the centrality of free and continuing consent; the relationship between sexual activity and legal institutions such as marriage; religious and cultural influences; and differences among national legal frameworks. It also examines how place, time, manner, and the characteristics of participants may affect legal classification. Comparative examples address minimum-age rules, public decency, prohibited family relationships, and selected judicial decisions from Canada, the United Kingdom, South Africa, and France. Finally, the essay distinguishes sexual reproduction from medically assisted reproduction and considers the limited but important contribution of forensic psychology. It argues that consent, bodily autonomy, equality, privacy, and protection against violence provide a useful transnational frame of reference, while the legal consequences of any particular act remain dependent on applicable domestic law and human-rights obligations.

detail.abstract: After the Taliban regained control of Afghanistan in August 2021, Afghan women began to experience further limitations on their educational opportunities, access to employment, ability to travel, freedom of speech, and participation in all forms of political activities. With the incremental tightening of these restrictions, conventional political and social avenues for participation have narrowed. Nonetheless, Afghan women persist in their forms of defiance against all these limitations. The present paper analyzes the impact of Taliban policies since 2021 on the types of resistance forms adopted by Afghan women. Furthermore, it seeks to investigate how political changes affect women’s strategies in their attempts to uphold their rights. The key finding points to the existence of resistance against rising repressions, although in forms unknown in the past and new channels of resistance have emerged. Namely, women have organized protests, underground and alternative education, digital activism, academic resistance, community initiatives, and transnational advocacy campaigns. The study substantiates the idea that the decline of political activity has pushed women to adapt their methods of resistance.

detail.abstract: The aim of this paper is to interpret horizontal fiscal equalization arrangements using the perspective of "entangled political economy." The entangled political economy approach emphasizes the emergent and interactional character of economic, fiscal, and political relationships. This perspective allows for a conceptualization of equalization as a network of actors interacting within a "sub-bazaar" field of negotiable fiscal-political exchanges. In addition to entanglements between central and state-local officials, equalization policymaking is demonstrated to incentivize participation by academics, consultancy firms, activists, and various other interested parties. Another relevant aspect of entangled political economy is the propagation of creative rhetorical justifications for certain equalization proposals. Equalization rhetoric not only has an objective of promoting public acceptance of negotiated equalization bargains amongst elitist sub-bazaar participants, but fundamentally it obscures the inherently political dimensions of equalization design and implementation. This paper introduces an entangled political economy approach with specific references to Australian equalization policy developments.

detail.abstract: Question answering tools over legislation are usually built once and evaluated once. The law then changes under them. This paper measures what that does to retrieval, using Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) and its amendment by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. The corpus is versioned by the date of the text: the original Official Journal text of 12 July 2024 and the consolidated text of 27 July 2026. On 11 questions that only the amended text can answer, hybrid retrieval over the stale corpus returns the right article number for 63.6% of questions but the current wording for 0.0%. On the current corpus the figures are 81.8% and 63.6%. Article-level hit rate hides a stale corpus. Cutting the text into one chunk per numbered paragraph raises full recall on the 33 original answerable questions from 69.7% to 75.8% and mean reciprocal rank from 0.790 to 0.843, and 90.9% of those questions retrieve a gold paragraph. Citation precision is 0.176 against a ceiling of 0.232 at six retrieved passages. The question set grows to 123, with every gold reference and quote checked by a program against the legal text; the 67 new questions are easier than the original 45. The LLM judge used to grade answers agrees with 41 hand labels on 82.9% of answers (Cohen's kappa 0.52), and accuracy is 66.7% strict and 69.7% lenient under either set of grades. Generation has not been rerun on the amended text. Code and results are released as an installable package.

detail.abstract: Agricultural value chains in developing countries connect a large number of smallholders to a small set of downstream buyers under weak contract enforcement. This review examines how two important features of these markets-buyer power and relational contracting-jointly shape prices, production, investment, and farmer welfare. We organize recent empirical evidence around a common framework linking farmers, intermediaries, and downstream buyers. Three main conclusions emerge. First, buyer power depends not only on the number of buyers but also on their conduct and farmers' ability to switch across buyers and activities. Second, market power at different stages of the value chain can interact in ways that make the effects of policy difficult to predict. Intermediaries may exercise market power while also providing valuable services, so higher farm-gate prices do not necessarily imply higher farmer welfare. Third, market power and relational contracting are closely connected: competition improves outside options but can also reduce the rents needed to sustain informal agreements. We argue that future work should study market power and relational contracting jointly and evaluate agricultural policies beyond their effects on prices alone.

detail.abstract: Portfolio performance evaluation is a crucial aspect of investment management analysis and is generally conducted by assessing risk-adjusted returns. This study analyzes the performance of worldwide equity mutual funds that use their national index as a financial benchmark during 1990 and 2024, employing metrics such as Alpha, adjusted Alpha, and the Sharpe, Sortino, and Treynor ratios. The findings indicate that the analyzed mutual funds have achieved positive risk-adjusted performance and have served as effective vehicles for tracking the index-whether for replication purposes or for use in hedging strategies involving financial derivatives. This article presents a novel study, given the volatile market conditions prevailing during the period under review.

detail.abstract:
This paper asks how well public card-spending data describe the revenue of Borsa Istanbul (BIST) companies, sector by sector, and whether changes in spending are associated with the companies’ stock returns. It is an association study. No trading rule, portfolio or performance measure is built or evaluated.
Every Thursday the Central Bank (TCMB) publishes domestic card spending for the previous week in 27 merchant category sectors, back to March 2014. I link 55 BIST companies in 14 groups to 13 of these sectors and compare card growth with quarterly revenue growth for 46 non-financial companies (2015Q2–2022Q3), and with inflation-adjusted revenue under IAS 29 for 2025. Because inflation explains most nominal spending growth(correlation 0.92 with CP Iinflation), every sector is examined in nominal, real and sector relative terms.
Card spending tracks revenue in every group, but how well differs widely. It explains 75% of the within-company variation in revenue growth for fuel distributors, 71% for grocery retailers, 62% for furniture makers, 57–58% for aviation, apparel and health, but only 7% for hotels and 14% for restaurants. Beyond inflation and the common cycle, the sector-specific part is strongest for fuel, furniture and grocery retail and is also significant for apparel, aviation, electronics and health. It is absent for food and beverage producers, whose revenue moves with card spending only through inflation, and weak for hotels, autos and telecom, where foreign guests, exporters’ sales, fleet sales and subscriptions are not captured by domestic cards. The first four weeks of a quarter already give most of the fit in retail, while aviation needs the whole quarter. Added to a firm’s own revenue history and inflation, card data give the largest out-of-sample reduction in forecast error for fuel (20%; Clark–West 𝑡 = 2.29, which does not survive Benjamini–Hochberg control across the twelve groups, 𝑞 = 0.13), and smaller, statistically in significant reductions for apparel (7%, 𝑡 = 1.28) and aviation (5%, 𝑡 = 1.23); for grocery retailers, where inflation already explains most of revenue growth, they add nothing. In electronics, card growth also leads next quarter’s revenue. Monthly arrivals and industrial-production data are weaker revenue proxies than card spending. A new source-verified geographic-sales check finds stronger real and sector-relative fits for exporters’ domestic revenue, but mixed nominal and forecast results; aligning Mavi’s card data to its fiscal quarters sharply raises its correlation.
Stock returns are not associated with the same data. Across 593weeklyreleases, five horizons and three return measures, none of 400 pooled stock-level tests survives Benjamini Hochberg control, and monthly Fama–MacBeth slopes are insignificant. Split by sector, two associations survive multiple-testing control: positive for electronics and appliances, where card data also lead revenue, and negative for hotels, which comes from the COVID years. The electronics result is the one link from spending to revenue to returns in the data; it rests on four stocks and one sector series. A BIST 100 association with total card growth on release days is already present before the 14:30 publication. Public weekly card data are a good, sector-specific nowcast of Turkish com pany sales, but not a source of return predictability.

detail.abstract: Nepal's electricity sector has undergone significant institutional transformation, from a government-operated system to a vertically integrated public utility with increasing private participation and specialized state-owned enterprises. Despite repeated reform initiatives, the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) continues to perform major functions in generation, transmission, system operation, distribution and electricity procurement. This working paper examines the historical evolution of Nepal's power sector, reviews institutional restructuring initiatives from 2000 to 2026, and assesses the rationale and alternative pathways for further unbundling of NEA. The study adopts a qualitative approach combining historical and policy analysis, a review of international reform experiences, and a preliminary assessment of Nepal's technical, financial and institutional characteristics. A systematic review of public debate and expert interviews are proposed to strengthen the subsequent analysis. Four institutional alternatives are examined: an improved vertically integrated utility, functional and accounting separation, a holding-company structure with subsidiaries, and independent corporate unbundling. The preliminary analysis identifies system-operation independence, transmission access, management of power purchase agreements, distribution financial viability and institutional coordination as key considerations. It also highlights that unbundling does not necessarily require privatization or competitive wholesale markets. The paper argues that restructuring should be evaluated against clearly defined sectoral objectives rather than pursued as an end in itself. Further empirical and stakeholder-based assessment is required to determine the appropriate degree and sequence of institutional separation for Nepal.

detail.abstract: Innovation in crop seeds is essential to sustain agricultural productivity growth, but the economic conditions supporting innovation also generate concerns about concentration and market power. This paper discusses the structural features of the modern seed industry and documents substantial concentration in seed sales, ownership of plant-variety intellectual property, and control of genetically engineered traits. Concentration alone, however, is a poor metric to assess competition in this context. Large fixed and sunk costs, product differentiation, effective intellectual property protection, and cumulative innovation imply that some degree of market power is intrinsic to the industry’s innovation process. The paper also reviews recent empirical structural models of differentiated-product seed markets that recover farmers’ willingness to pay for genetically engineered traits and quantify the distribution of innovation benefits between farmers and seed companies. The licensing of genetically engineered traits among competitors is also discussed. Counterfactual evidence indicates that observed outcomes remain far from full industry collusion, while also revealing the potentially severe consequences of monopolization given the very inelastic aggregate demand for seeds. The analysis highlights the industry-specific fundamentals of market structure and the tension between market power and the dynamic incentives for innovation.

title: Commons Capitalism and the Institutional Economics of Worker Well-Being

detail.title: Commons Capitalism and the Institutional Economics of Worker Well-Being

detail.abstract:
Workers can devote decades to building an enterprise of considerable economic strength and still confront serious personal adversity with resources limited to their wages, savings, and ordinary employment benefits. Commons Capitalism proposes that the institution itself should help bear that burden. A Commons Capitalism Entity (CCE) deliberately accumulates productive capital, financial reserves, and organizational capabilities to improve workers' lives and to come to their aid when illness, disability, caregiving, or household emergencies threaten their economic security, even when those events have no connection with work. The CCE combines a nonmember, nonshareholder, nonprofit Commons Corporation, market-facing Subsidiaries, four constitutionally designated funds, intergenerational capital stewardship, and acquisitions intended specifically to bring more workers into its protection. Research on institutional ownership, healthcare financial protection, and paid family leave supports important mechanisms underlying this proposal. The distinctive proposition is that a commercially viable enterprise can adopt a continuing directive to provide reasonable assistance with private precarity, subject to need, available resources, equitable procedures, and intergenerational stewardship, rather than leaving that assistance to occasional acts of generosity. This affirmative account introduces the forthcoming companion paper, Commons Capitalism and the Worker-Capital Chasm.

The concepts, institutional architecture, and substantive arguments concerning Commons Capitalism were developed and directed by the author. AI-assisted material was reviewed, revised as appropriate, and approved by the author, who independently evaluated and verified factual claims and scholarly references and accepts full responsibility for the paper.

detail.abstract:
This study evaluates the predictive limits of machine learning architectures within highly volatile digital asset regimes by forecasting stationary log returns rather than non-stationary raw price levels. To bypass standard look-ahead bias and identity function vulnerabilities common in applied financial machine learning, we construct a forecasting engine utilizing five years of daily historical Ethereum (ETH-USD) market metrics spanning January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2025. Given that Ethereum's real-world all-time high occurred historically in November 2021, metrics generated during the 2025 out-of-sample window are formally treated as part of a simulated evaluation framework to test model performance limits under high market noise. Descriptive statistical analysis identified an absolute absence of a linear relationship (correlation coefficient of -0.01) between daily log trading volume and asset returns. A Random Forest Regressor was trained on a chronological data split (2021–2024) and evaluated against an out-of-sample testing window spanning the full year of 2025.

Benchmarked against a 7-Day Simple Moving Average (SMA), empirical results demonstrated that the baseline 7-Day SMA achieved a superior Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.029914, outperforming the Random Forest model's error of 0.031403. A formal Diebold-Mariano statistical significance test yielded a test statistic of -0.9383 with a corresponding p-value of 0.3481. Because the p-value sits significantly above the standard academic threshold of 0.05, the null hypothesis of equal predictive accuracy cannot be rejected. These findings present a valuable academic null result, proving that when forced to forecast true stationary daily log returns, classical rolling statistical benchmarks can systematically out-predict complex non-linear machine learning architectures.

detail.abstract: We ask whether a Pareto-efficient and strategy-proof school assignment rule must coincide with top trading cycles if it is stable whenever top trading cycles is stable. We call this property initial-stability rigidity and compare it with robust minimal instability under capacity-residual stability comparisons. With two schools of capacities (𝑄, 1), both properties hold under exactly the same priority condition: the relative priority permutation avoids the patterns 231 and 321, and every rotated interval block of length at least four ends by rank 𝑄 + 1. With three schools, the properties separate. The smallest mixed-capacity structure separating them has five students and total capacity four. In a family with 𝑛 ≥ 3 students and capacities (𝑄, 1, 1), 𝑄 ≥ 2, robust minimal instability always holds, whereas rigidity holds exactly when 𝑄 ≥ 𝑛-2. Finally, every two-school projection can satisfy both properties while the full structure satisfies neither. A single adjacent priority exchange produces this change in an infinite family.

detail.abstract: We study whether stock disclosures by recognizable investors generate abnormal market reactions beyond the reactions produced by comparable but nonrecognizable managers. We define the Buffett effect as the incremental abnormal return to a disclosed new position that is attributable to the public recognition of the disclosing investor. We construct a recognition index from Wikipedia pageviews and ProQuest news mentions. Using data from 2000 to 2025 we compare market reaction to disclosures of 24 recognizable discretionary funds with disclosures of 24 matched control funds. New-position disclosures by recognizable managers generate a positive disclosure premium over the filing date and the following trading days, and the premium increases with investor recognition. We construct calendar-time portfolios that mechanically copy each group's disclosed purchases and find that copying the most recognized investors earns a significant alpha that persists for months and does not reverse. The evidence is most consistent with an entangled attention-information channel: investor recognition directs scarce investor attention toward selected disclosures, and the information revealed in those disclosures is then capitalized into prices.

detail.abstract: Traditional internal audit routines in public utilities face increasing demands to shift toward more risk-focused approaches. This study assessed the transition from pre-audit to risk-based internal audit practices of a Philippine electric cooperative. A quantitative, descriptive-correlational census design included all 56 accessible qualified personnel. The study used an expert-validated, pilot-tested questionnaire and analyzed the data using descriptive statistics and Pearson productmoment correlation. The findings showed that the cooperative has well-established pre-audit practices and favorable conditions to adopt risk-based internal auditing (RBIA). Moreover, organizational, personnel competency, resource, and technology factors were generally perceived as conditions that may facilitate or hinder RBIA adoption. Consequently, the findings revealed a moderate, statistically significant positive relationship between existing pre-audit practices and readiness to adopt RBIA. The study also identified management-related concerns, changes in audit processes, knowledge and skills, organizational arrangements, and resource and technology limitations as serious challenges that need to be addressed. Theoretically, the findings reinforce Institutional Theory by showing that established pre-audit practices can be adapted toward an RBIA approach through risk integration in audit planning, formalizing RBIA policies and guidelines, strengthening internal audit personnel competencies, clarifying audit roles and responsibilities, providing adequate staffing and resources, improving access to reliable and timely information, and enhancing technological support. The suggested framework will serve as a practical guide for transitioning from the existing pre-audit approach to RBIA. This will help cooperative leaders strengthen risk management, internal control, governance, and decision-making while building on existing audit practices.

detail.abstract: Option analytics platforms label the strikes with the largest open-interest gamma exposure (GEX) as "call walls" and "put walls" and present them as intraday resistance and support. We test this claim on Nasdaq-100 index options (NDX and NDXP) over 124 sessions from 12 January to 10 July 2026, using a pre-registered design (OSF, osf.io/9scfn) that compares walls with placebo levels matched on distance from spot. Once price reaches them, walls are breached somewhat less often than placebos (call walls 16.9% vs 23.8%; put walls 15.0% vs 22.5%), but neither difference is significant (p = 0.115 and 0.135). The confidence intervals exclude reductions of 20 percentage points or more, the threshold registered in advance, while remaining compatible with substantial effects. A pre-registered fade trade at the wall shows no evidence of profit: its mean net result is −4.0 (call walls) and −2.3 (put walls) NQ points per trade, with wide intervals spanning zero. The pre-registered verdict is "no large edge". Secondary, uncorrected measures suggest price lingers somewhat longer near walls. We also show that walls sit closer to spot than lower-ranked GEX strikes, which biases comparisons based on how often levels are reached, and we document the limits of OPRA and open-interest data for this question, including that once-a-day open interest cannot see intraday 0DTE positioning. title: Who Writes "We the People"? International Human Rights Law and the Legality of Constituent Processes

detail.title: Who Writes "We the People"? International Human Rights Law and the Legality of Constituent Processes

detail.abstract: Every modern constitution opens in the voice of the people, yet international law has never asked, in doctrinal terms, whether the people lawfully held the pen. This Article argues that constitution making is an exercise of public power that obligations the state already carries govern stage by stage. Read through Article 31 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties and General Comment No. 25, Articles 1, 2, 19, 21, 25, and 27 of the ICCPR, Articles 1 and 13(1) of the ICESCR, Article 7 of CEDAW, and Article 5(c) of CERD yield a chain of ten process rights, from self-determination to effective remedy, each attached to an identified stage of the constituent process. The Article converts that chain into an analytical legal frame, a three-step test of attachment, specification, and breach, governed by two principles. Volume neutrality holds that the law measures legality, not mobilization. Non-cure holds that a plebiscite cannot launder an assembly elected under an unequal rule. The frame joins constitutional theory (Sieyès, Schmitt, Arato), design scholarship (Elster, Landau, Dixon and Landau), and empirical work (Ginsburg, Elkins, and Blount; Eisenstadt, LeVan, and Maboudi) to the international law of participation (Franck, Fox, Hart). The Article meets its strongest adversaries, among them Marshall v. Canada, Moohan v. United Kingdom, and the Venezuelan Supreme Court’s 1999 surrender to a “most sovereign” assembly. It draws support from Doctors for Life, the South African Certification Judgments, Colombia’s substitution doctrine, the Inter-American Court’s Advisory Opinion OC-28/21, and Article 10(2) of the African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance. Six constituent processes test the frame. Venezuela turned roughly sixty percent of the vote into ninety-five percent of the seats. Bolivia approved its text while elected delegates could not enter the chamber. Switzerland ratified its 1999 revision by a double majority, and Chile seated the first gender-parity convention and then lawfully refused two texts. The education obligation of Article 13(1) of the ICESCR emerges as the point where doctrine and evidence converge, and the one states most often neglect. Legality cannot promise a good constitution. It promises that a people settles its constituent moment by counting, not by force.

detail.abstract: A sequential model confidence set eliminates a model once the evidence that it is not among the best reaches 1/α. I ask how this evidence should be aggregated across the rivals of a model, and how fast elimination can be. For losses in [0, 1], every loss-based certificate that a model is not best is dominated by the wealth of a bettor who stakes on the model losing to a predictable aggregate of its rivals; the construction in use, an average of pairwise e-processes, aggregates outside the bet, by exponential weighting over pairwise bettors. For i.i.d. streams, no loss-based procedure with distribution-free validity eliminates a model that is not best in fewer expected rounds than log(1/α) divided by the relative entropy from the data law to the laws under which the model is best. This instance-wise limit carries no correction for the number of models, and a universal portfolio of rivals, which learns from the stream, attains it as α → 0, with a non-asymptotic bound read off from its regret. Uniformly over the placement of one better rival among K rivals that tie the model, however, every valid procedure must pay log K in the threshold, the price of model-selection aggregation, and exponential weighting attains this minimax price. Merging pairwise e-processes by any admissible rule cannot exceed the rate of the best single rival, and averaging them pays about the logarithm of the number of rivals in the threshold at every instance with few better rivals, a cost I bound non-asymptotically and show to be tight to first order. For small gaps the rate loss is a squared ratio of Sharpe ratios; it equals 2K/(K + 1) when K rivals beat the model by equal gaps and all losses have equal variances and correlations, and it is unbounded in general. Two practical certificates, a plug-in Kelly portfolio and a universal portfolio over the leading rivals, are valid under any dependence, exact on fixed evaluation sets and compatible with closed testing. On hyperparameter searches over five tabular data sets and three language-model leaderboards with up to 220 models, the plug-in portfolio eliminates models faster than the pairwise construction with the same stakes and guarantees, by a median factor between 1.23 and 1.46 at α = 0.05, and never significantly later; the advantage persists down to α = 0.001 and shrinks as α decreases, as expected of a threshold effect.

detail.abstract: This book length study argues that Amman's future should be perceived not as mere expansion but as the construction of an integrated metropolitan system, where heritage sites like the Citadel and Roman Theatre are viewed as connected components of a dynamic cultural network rather than isolated locations. It redefines urban governance as a design discipline, suggesting that the city's topographical context should inform a new conceptual framework to guide its transformation into a connected and accessible metropolis, with vital functions such as connectivity, resilience, and cultural continuity serving as indicators of urban performance. The recommended Metropolitan Intelligence Observatory would use a topographically adjusted accessibility measure to assess urban vitality and connectivity, ensuring that interventions enhance overall quality of life and integrate various systems without compromising other functions. Furthermore, drawing on examples from other cities, the approach emphasizes the importance of understanding local context to create governance that adapts to Amman's unique urban landscape, thereby fostering social inclusivity and environmental sustainability. As a political capital Amman is incomplete with a standardized building vocabulary, as a hillside urban connurbia it is non-described, and as an Arab city more of the same.

title: Sovereign Sight, Painted Knowledge: An Unexamined Corpus of Identifiable Cartographic Content in Habsburg Court Painting, 1560 to 1700

detail.title: Sovereign Sight, Painted Knowledge: An Unexamined Corpus of Identifiable Cartographic Content in Habsburg Court Painting, 1560 to 1700

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: none
declarations.funderStatement: self

detail.abstract: Between the mid-sixteenth and late seventeenth centuries, the Spanish Habsburg monarchy and its regents in the Southern Netherlands commissioned and collected paintings that contain a rich and largely unexamined body of identifiable cartographic material: globes, wall maps, nautical charts, and topographic views rendered with sufficient fidelity to permit source identification. This article establishes that corpus and reads it as evidence for a historical process at the center of the Habsburg information order: the circulation of geographic knowledge out of the cartographic workshops of the Southern Netherlands and into the sovereign knowledge system of the Iberian monarchy. It surveys the paintings, concentrating on works held in the Museo del Prado, the Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien, and El Escorial; it reviews the scholarship on scientific and cartographic objects in Flemish gallery painting and on the cartographic institutions of the Spanish monarchy, identifying a gap concerning the spatial content of these objects; and it undertakes qualitative source identification, in the tradition James Welu established for Vermeer and extended here for the first time to the Habsburg court corpus, for the terrestrial globe in Jan Brueghel the Elder and Peter Paul Rubens's Allegory of Sight, painted in 1617 for the Archdukes Albert and Isabella, and for the maritime chart in Adriaen Stalbemt and Frans Francken II's The Sciences and the Arts. The argument is that the cartographic objects displayed in the spaces of Habsburg sovereignty occupied a different position within the early modern information order than the commercial wall maps of the Dutch domestic interior, and that the difference is a recoverable trace of how geographic knowledge moved, and was withheld, between the commercial map trade and the sovereign court. The article closes by specifying the spatial research program that would test this claim quantitatively; a program whose protocol is developed in a companion methods study and whose execution requires sustained archival collaboration now underway. The purpose here is to make the corpus visible, to establish the historical case for reading it as evidence about the circulation and control of sovereign knowledge, and to specify what a subsequent spatial analysis would have to show.

detail.abstract: Public associations increasingly participate in service delivery, policy implementation, and collaborative governance. However, less attention has been paid to how administrative arrangements shape organisational conditions for participation. The article develops the Regulatory-Autonomy-Capacity (RAC) framework to examine this relationship. The study uses a conceptual design drawing on public administration and governance literature, European freedom of association standards, European Court of Human Rights judgments, and the Ukrainian regulatory context. The framework links administrative arrangements, organisational autonomy, and capacity. Administrative arrangements are examined through proportionality, predictability, and accessibility; autonomy through strategic and operational discretion; and capacity through resource mobilisation, professional competence, stakeholder coordination, and organisational adaptability. The analysis suggests that administrative arrangements may influence capacity by shaping autonomy, but autonomy alone does not determine capacity or governance outcomes. These depend on resources, professional competences, institutional openness, and collaborative relationships. Ukraine serves as an illustrative context of administrative reform, not a representative European case.

detail.abstract: The attainment of economic liberties for women, including the ability of married women to acquire, use, and transfer property without the consent of their husbands, is a historically recent achievement. The objective of this paper is to indicate how "voice" mechanisms of communication were implicated in engendering institutional change equipping married women with property rights in the U.S. Whereas certain studies emphasize the contributions of American proto feminists in articulating gendered rights claims with respect to property, an entangled political economy approach alternatively illustrates the interactions of multiple actors in negotiating women's improving access to property rights. Married women's property rights reform was, in effect, an iterative process involving complex communicative strategies and techniques. Supporters of property rights reform for married women used their voices to facilitate group sensemaking about gendered economic deprivations, combining this with anti-stigma narratives surrounding the positive consequences, as well as moral propriety, of extending property rights. An "institutional catallaxy" of property rights reform was also shaped by contentious communicative interactions with reform opponents through legislative and judicial branches of U.S. state governments. This study indicates how voice mechanisms informed key institutional changes affecting the rights of women and broader economic relations between the sexes.

detail.abstract: The exposure of smallholder farmers to crop losses, fluctuation of income and difficulties in getting credit to finance their farming practices have all intensified with time, as a result of climate shocks. The risks can be more widespread than the farm household they affect, and can impact financial institutions with a high concentration of agricultural loans that are at risk of loss if residents are unable to repay. One possible solution to such risks is to insure against them based on the credit and lines of production in the agricultural sector and automatically be paid out when some weather conditions like low rainfall or floods are experienced beyond a predetermined threshold. However, there can be neutralization of these structures by basis risk, financial attributes of the household and borrower differentiated climate and repayment riskiness. The paper discusses the possibility to avert agricultural credit risk where exposed to climate change by credit-linked weather-index microinsurance, and how it is plausible to use econometric and machine-learning tools to filter out susceptible borrowers to insurance and repayment risk. The empirical analysis is an amalgamation of household attributes, which pertain to agriculture and microinsurance and climate and weather, financial and transactional conditions, and basis risk. The probability of a relevant outcome of credit or insurance risk and the marginal effects of these outcomes are calculated using a Probit regression model. A parallel machine-learning classification model is built which then categorizes borrowers under perceived risk profiles and measures the performance of the model. Comparisons manifold: the statistical inference and predictive performance are compared using sufficient measures, including the measures of classification accuracy and precision, recall and F1-score, ROC-AUC among other measure performance-relevant measures. Following the empirical analysis of the data set, facts about coefficients, marginal effects and forecast outcomes will be reported. The lessons rely on the findings and are aimed to provide evidence of how the insurance and credit functions could be combined to enable climate-risk management of ag finance to smallholder.

detail.abstract: Automating the containerization, Kubernetes orchestration and CI/CD of heterogeneous software repositories is challenging, due to the diversity of underlying tools for source analysis, cloud-native synthesis and verification. Unconstrained Generative AI assistants may introduce insecure or unbuildable configurations, as root execution, missing health checks, unpinned base images or misconfigured clouds deployments. Here we report the Autonomous AI DevSecOps Platform, a multi-agent system orchestrated by a strongly-typed directed acyclic graph (DAG) using the LangGraph framework. The system has several agents that communicate using a shared, typed schema (PipelineState): (1) a repository scraper, that analyzes the source tree in less than one second (0.65s) and extract manifests; (2) a container and Kubernetes synthesizer applying CIS Docker Benchmark v1.6.0 standards, runs non-root UID 1001 images and generate Kubernetes Helm charts respecting the Pod Security Standards (PSS Restricted profile); (3) a Docker validator that makes linting, loopback network probes and selfhealing capabilities with a bounded number of retries (K_max=2) and (4) a multi-cloud CI/CD agent, that generates GitHub Container Registry (GHCR), AWS ECR/EKS, GCP Artifact Registry/GKE and Azure ACR/AKS manifests with integrated shift-left security gates (Gitleaks, Semgrep, Trivy), SBOM generation (Syft), cryptographic signing (Sigstore Cosign) and a deterministic three-tier template fallback engine. We evaluated the system using 142 automated tests and 74 sub-tests achieving a full pass-rate (100%) in 7.27 seconds. By construction, the system guarantees the YAML language syntactic validity using PyYAML, avoiding targeted container security smells and enforces run isolation. This work contributes an open-source solution bridging the gap between Generative AI reasoning and production-grade cloud-native systems.

detail.abstract:
Copyright law is famously described in ex post terms. Much emphasis is placed on the doctrine's various uncertainties, resolved only after lengthy and expensive litigation. Few have considered the role that the billion-dollar entertainment insurance industry might play in reversing this typical narrative. Elsewhere, insurance law scholars have long acknowledged insurance's role as an ex ante regulatory tool, complementing or even supplanting government oversight in industries as diverse from policing to corporate governance. This Essay argues that in the creative industry, too, insurance acts as a form of ex ante copyright: a regulatory tool within the copyright system that can, if designed correctly, provide greater certainty and facilitate, rather than chill, creativity up front. 

The very availability of insurance increases the well-documented phenomenon of moral hazard, or, greater risk-taking. Yet, and unlike in other areas such as auto, health, or fire insurance, creative moral hazard might be positive, exhibiting a counteracting force to a variety of uncertain ex post chilling copyright doctrines. And while the typical role of the insurer is to reduce moral hazard, the changing landscape of content liability insurance--for example, that insurers are increasingly more willing to issue policies based on fair use rather than requiring licenses--evinces the uniqueness of copyright infringement torts, in which complete reduction has never been, nor should be, the goal. Studying the evolution of liability insurance in the content industries is also instructive for general insurance law scholarship, as it suggests that there may be some torts, like copyright infringement, for which there is an optimal level of tortious conduct and, in turn, some optimal level of moral hazard.
